Subject: Initial MSA + Order Form — technical clarifications and signer

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — team was impressed with the latency numbers. We're trying to move the contracting piece forward this week. I'm attaching the Order Form and a short SOW appendix with the workloads we expect. A few quick asks so legal can scope their redlines: 

- Can you confirm whether Redwood's MSA covers data residency restrictions for EU data (we may have a subset of EU customers routed to EU-only infra)?
- On the order form, we flagged the per-token billing cadence and the seat-based baseline; we'd like a simple example for month 1 vs month 3 billing to share with finance.
- Who at Redwood is authorized to sign the Order Form? We usually need a named individual (title + signer authority) to route internally.

Also attaching our standard contract packet in case that speeds review. If possible we'd like an initial set of redlines back by EOD Friday (the procurement team is trying to close internal approvals).

Appreciate it —
Lisa

Head of Platform Partnerships
Vectra Analytics

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-08-12T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Initial MSA + Order Form — technical clarifications and signer

Naomi / Marcus —

Thanks for the heads up, Naomi. Quick intake from legal: 

1) Data residency: Redwood's standard hosted MSA does not guarantee EU-only routing by default. For EU-only flows we need either Redwood Private (VPC) or a Dedicated region pinning clause. I recommend we propose a "Data Residency Annex" in the MSA that:
   - Commits to process EU customer data in EU regions only for the subset of traffic they identify,
   - Specifies certification scope (e.g., ISO/SOC specifics for that infra) and any additional costs.

2) Billing example: I'll draft a short table showing how token billing + seat baseline would manifest across month 1 (pilot) and month 3 (ramp). Naomi, can you confirm expected pilot team size + conservative token estimate for month 3? I'll include the table in the reply.

3) Signer authority: Redwood's authorization matrix: VP+ for commercial value > $250k ARR; Director+ for < $250k. For speed I'd propose we offer: "Authorized Signatory: VP, Commercial Partnerships (or delegate)" and then follow up with the named person when procurement asks. If Vectra needs a named individual now, we can name: Marissa Cole, VP Commercial — happy to be the listed signer.

4) Redlines: I'll do a first-pass redline on the Order Form and flag MSA clauses that need legal review (indemnity, data processing addendum, termination for convenience, liability caps). Expect initial tracker back by EOD.

Questions for sales:
- Naomi: confirm pilot SKU and expected monthly token volume for month 3.
- Marcus: any known constraints on our side re: residency (capacity in EU region / Dedicated availability)?

I'll attach a short summary + redline tracker once done.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference
From: Evan Soto <evan.soto@vectra.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lisa Carter <lisa.carter@vectra.ai>, contracts@vectra.ai
Date: 2026-08-13T08:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial MSA + Order Form — technical clarifications and signer

Thanks Naomi / Kimberly. Quick answers from Vectra side: 

- Pilot team size: 6 engineers + 2 product analysts. Estimated token usage in pilot month: ~25M tokens (dev + internal testing). Month 3 conservative estimate: ~120M tokens.
- Residency: We need EU-only processing for EU customers' PII. Non-EU traffic can go to default Redwood hosted. We are open to Dedicated capacity if that's easier to guarantee.
- Signer: Procurement prefers a named signer. If Marissa is acceptable, please list her and we'll start internal routing. If Redwood prefers to leave generic we can still start but procurement will likely request a named signatory before sending PO.

We've also attached a short procurement checklist — main gating items are DPA + SOC2 evidence and signatory name.

Evan
Evan Soto
Senior Procurement Manager
Vectra Analytics

Hi Lisa / Evan —

Thanks for the quick responses and the token estimates — that's helpful. Next steps from Redwood: 

1) Legal (Kimberly) will send a redline tracker with: a recommended Data Residency Annex (two options: Dedicated pinning vs service-level data residency commitment), proposed edits to indemnity/cap caps, and a draft DPA reference. Expect that in ~4 business hours.

2) Commercial/Finance: I'll send a simple billing example table (pilot vs month 3) and a short note on seat baseline + overage math in a follow-up email.

3) Signatory: Marissa Cole is fine to list as the authorized signatory for initial routing. Marissa — confirming you're OK to be listed for this counterparty? We'll update to "Marissa Cole, VP, Commercial Partnerships" on the signature block.

4) Attachments: attaching the redline tracker and SOW comments once legal finishes.

Proposed mutual action plan: 
- 2026-08-14 EOD (today): Redwood sends initial redlines + billing example + signer confirmation
- 2026-08-16: Vectra returns counter-redlines and procurement packet
- 2026-08-19: Target final MSA + Order Form for signature

If that timeline is tight for you, let me know and we can extend by a few days.

Thanks everyone —
